'''''Xanthium orientale''''' is a species of annual plant of the daisy family [[Asteraceae]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Xanthium orientale L. {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:260872-1 |access-date=2022-07-01 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref>

==Use by Native Americans==
The [[Zuni people]] use the plant for multiple purposes. The chewed seeds are rubbed onto the body before the cactus ceremony to protect it from spines. A compound [[poultice]] of seeds is applied to wounds or used to remove splinters.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Stevenson |first=Matilda Coxe |date=1915 |title=Ethnobotany of the Zuni Indians |journal=SI-BAE Annual Report |volume=30 |pages=62–63}}</ref> The seeds are also ground, mixed with cornmeal, made into cakes, and steamed for food.{{sfnp|Stevenson|1915|p=71}}<ref>{{cite journal|last=Castetter |first=Edward F. |date=1935 |title=Ethnobiological Studies in the American Southwest I. Uncultivated Native Plants Used as Sources of Food |journal=University of New Mexico Bulletin |volume=4|issue=1|pages=1–44, 54}}</ref>
